body.statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, a polynomial system given by straight-line programs and satisfying the reduced regular-sequence hypothesis away from a supplied inequation admits a probabilistic Gröbner-free geometric-resolution algorithm. On successful generic choices, the algorithm represents the relevant zero-dimensional section by a primitive element, its monic polynomial, and rational coordinate parametrizations, with arithmetic complexity polynomial in the straight-line-program evaluation length and the geometric degrees of the successive varieties.

source.locator: main geometric-resolution complexity theorem and the reduced regular-sequence hypothesis
